description: Generalized End-to-End speaker verification loss for balanced batches of normalized embeddings, using leave-one-out positive centroids, full negative centroids, and either the softmax or hardest-negative contrast objective (paper §1 Eq. (1), §2.1 Eqs. (4)–(10)); loss kwargs are dispatched by src/topologies/training/losses.py:196-200.

examples.code:
import tempfile
import torch
from topologies import Trainer, build, synth
root = tempfile.mkdtemp()
@synth.generator
def samples(ctx):
    features = torch.randn(4, generator=ctx.rng.torch)
    return {"features": synth.Tensor(features), "labels": int(ctx.index) % 2}
dataset = synth.Spec("ge2e-speakers", generator=samples, size=8, splits={"train": 1.0}, seed=7, root=root, monitor="none").run()
train = dataset.for_recipe("tabular-classify", split="train")
model = build("mlp", "tiny", in_features=4, out_features=3)
trainer = Trainer(model, train, recipe="tabular-classify", recipe_config={"loss": "ge2e", "loss_kwargs": {"objective": "softmax"}}, batch_size=8, max_epochs=1, device="cpu")
trainer.fit()
examples.title: Train speaker embeddings with GE2E

name: Generalized End-to-End speaker verification loss

parameters.additional parameters: objective, w, and b are the only accepted parameters in **params; unsupported keys raise ValueError
parameters.b: finite real scalar or floating-point tensor scalar bias (default -5.0)
parameters.ignore_index: must be None because ignored speaker IDs are incompatible with balanced batches
parameters.logits_or_prediction: floating-point raw embeddings shaped [B, D] with positive B and D; B must contain at least two speakers with the same number of utterances per speaker
parameters.reduction: none returns one loss per utterance in input order, mean averages utterances, or sum totals utterances (default mean)
parameters.targets: integer speaker IDs shaped [B], with at least two speakers and at least two utterances per speaker in a balanced batch
parameters.w: finite positive real scalar or floating-point tensor scalar scale (default 10.0); tensor values may receive gradients
